title: Commitment splitter and invoice mapping guidelines for multi-entity customers
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Several enterprise customers and marketplace partners have requested the ability to split committed spend across multiple legal entities, cost centers, or marketplace offsets at invoice time. Current Redwood billing emits a single invoice per account/contract and lacks a deterministic mapping flow for multi-entity settlements, which forces manual finance work and delays renewals.

Goal: Produce a concise, operational playbook and decision ruleset that product, sales operations, and engineering can use to implement automated commitment-splitting and invoice mapping. The playbook should: 1) define deterministic priority rules for how incoming usage and commitments map to invoices and cost centers; 2) surface edge cases and default fallbacks; 3) provide examples for common customer topologies (multi-entity, reseller marketplace, hybrid commitments + pay-as-you-go); and 4) include acceptance criteria and instrumentation targets for rollout.

Scope: This ticket covers policy and routing rules (non-technical) and mapping to the billing schema that ENG will implement. Implementation of the automated splitter and downstream invoice generation is tracked in ENG-18821.

Out of scope: Pricing algorithm changes, invoice formatting copy, tax calculation logic, and policy for refunds/credits beyond allocation rules (handled in separate legal/finance tasks).
acceptance_criteria: A documented decision matrix that covers at least 6 customer archetypes and maps each to a deterministic invoice allocation outcome.
A set of default fallback rules when metadata is incomplete (e.g., assign to primary contract then to headcount-based cost center).
Clear set of labels/metadata fields that must be present on the contract (e.g., cost_center_id, entity_id, marketplace_offset) and spec for validation errors.
A set of test cases (examples) that ENG can use in the billing integration test harness with pass/fail expectations.
Stakeholder signoff from Sales Ops, Finance, Legal, and Engineering on the policy document.
triage_matrix: Priority rules in order: 1) Explicit invoice_splits defined on the contract metadata. 2) If absent, use per-invoice allocation configured on the renewal (sales-provided allocation table). 3) If still absent, route to the contract primary entity and append a marketplace offset line if marketplace usage detected. 4) For legacy contracts with multiple linked entities, use 'last configured allocation' with a time-bound audit trail requirement.
decision_flow: 1. Evaluate incoming usage record: identify contract_id, org_metadata, and marketplace_tag. 2. If invoice_splits present -> apply splits in order listed (validate percentages sum to 100). 3. Else if sales allocation table present -> apply. 4. Else if marketplace_tag=true -> create invoice lines for reseller entity and marketplace offset line item on primary contract. 5. Else default to primary_entity. 6. Emit allocation audit record and surface allocation preview in Console before invoice finalization for contracts flagged 'preview_required'.
examples: Customer A (single contract, 3 cost centers): sales provided allocation table -> create one invoice per cost center with allocated usage; invoice references parent contract and shows allocation percentages.
Customer B (marketplace reseller): usage arrives with marketplace_tag -> invoice to reseller entity; create marketplace_offset credit line against platform contract for settlement reconciliation.
Customer C (multi-entity, no allocation metadata): fallback to primary contract entity for all usage; tag invoice with 'allocation_missing' for Finance follow-up.
Customer D (renewal with new splits): system uses the allocation effective_date on contract metadata to determine which allocation applies to usage in a given billing period.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misallocated spend causing finance disputes. Mitigation: require explicit signoff on allocation tables for high-value customers and provide allocation preview in Console.
Risk: Unknown metadata leading to silent defaulting. Mitigation: emit allocation_missing tag and create automated support tickets for contracts above threshold amount.
Risk: Marketplace settlement mismatch. Mitigation: include marketplace_offset lines and reconciliation report exported weekly for Finance.
Risk: Implementation delays impacting renewals. Mitigation: provide manual interim process for Sales Ops and prioritize top-10 impacted customers.
metrics_and_signals: Reduction in manual finance allocation interventions (baseline: 12/month) -> target < 3/month after rollout.
% invoices with allocation_missing tag -> target < 2% of enterprise invoices.
Time to invoice generation for split contracts (median) -> target < 2 hours processing time for allocation pass.
Number of allocation validation failures (per week) and time to resolution (SLA 72h).
notes: This playbook is intentionally implementation-agnostic. ENG will convert the rules into schema changes and allocation microservice behavior. We will iterate on edge cases after a controlled rollout to top enterprise customers.
